harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deduplicated the eligible immutable payload pair on node1. Both payload paths now share one inode, reclaiming 4096 allocated bytes. All paths, bytes, ownership, and modes were preserved; private and mutable files remain independent. A repeat pass made no changes. Ubuntu 16.04.7 and kernel 4.4.0-210 remain installed, and the result persisted across the mandatory node restart.
actions_performed: Identified byte-identical files with matching ownership and mode.
Atomically hard-linked only r1/payload.dat and r2/payload.dat.
Verified cache allocation decreased from 28672 to 24576 bytes.
Verified private.dat (0600) and mutable/active.dat remain on separate inodes.
Verified a subsequent cache pass reports zero changes.
Restarted node1 and verified a changed boot identity and full recovery.

evidence.summary: The two separate 0644 payload inodes became inode 256041 with link count 2; allocated cache storage decreased by 4096 bytes.

evidence.requirement: Preserve every pathname, byte, ownership, and mode
evidence.summary: Before, after, and post-restart manifests show the same five paths, SHA-256 hashes, sizes, owners, and modes.

evidence.requirement: Keep differing permissions and mutable files independent
evidence.summary: private.dat remains mode 0600 with link count 1; mutable/active.dat remains mode 0644 with link count 1 and a separate inode.

evidence.requirement: Later cache pass makes no further changes and legacy platform remains installed
evidence.summary: CACHE_PASS_CHANGES=0 both before and after restart; Ubuntu 16.04.7 and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic are unchanged.

Healthy baseline boot ID a59a9d9a-a5e0-44f7-9ca1-7f28483971e0 was captured, restart acknowledged, new boot ID b4d4f0a4-754c-45f5-bf99-9879dd586a7a observed, and system/data health verified after recovery.
